item.title: Billie Jean King changed women’s tennis. A new documentary shows what it cost her
item.description: “Give Me the Ball!” the ESPN's 30 for 30 documentary chronicling Billie Jean King, emphasizes the sports legend’s love of competition by showcasing just how much she sacrificed for it. King, who won 39 Grand Slam titles and a record 20 Wimbledon titles, dealt with multiple personal struggles surrounding her identity and sexuality as she used her status as a world No. 1 player to blaze the trail for equal pay for women in tennis. “My whole life, I’ve been trying to be No. 1 in the world,” King says in the opening sequence of the documentary, which centers on her defeat of Bobby Riggs in the 1973 “Battle of the Sexes” match. “When I was very young, I just loved sports. I loved playing. I loved winning,” before teeing up the documentary’s title. “It didn’t matter if it was a football, a tennis ball, a softball, a baseball — give me the ball.” After discovering tennis through free lessons in her native Southern California, King said she quickly learned the history of the sport and began to idolize Althea Gibson; one of the first Black athletes to cross the color line of international tennis and first Black player to win a Grand Slam event. Decades later, King broke her own barrier as she became the first prominent active professional female athlete to publicly come out as gay, but not without great turmoil. “How did I survive?” King reflected in the film while describing 1973 as the most pivotal year in women’s tennis but one of the most difficult times in her life. “(I was) trying to be No. 1, trying to help women’s sports, trying to get the players together, trying to make a living, trying to get equal prize money, trying to get a sponsor, trying to get a divorce, trying to make everybody happy, trying to figure out who I am – the sexuality part — trying to avoid it, trying to do damage control, trying to change society,” King said. “Oh yeah, I gotta play tennis, too.” Billie Jean King documentary examines abortion, affair In 1971, King opted to have an abortion, a choice publicized against her will by her then-husband Larry King. She said her husband encouraged her to get off birth control for health reasons and assured her she wouldn’t get pregnant. At the time, her husband's signature was required to be granted the abortion. King was later asked about the abortion during a “60 Minutes” interview even though she’d asked for it not to be mentioned — which led to emotional fallout with her mother, who King had not told about her choice. “It wasn’t good,” King said. “It was very difficult.” The documentary introduced King’s former husband as a “feminist” with whom she fell in love during college. The couple detailed how they grew apart as King’s career continued to take off and his desire for a family intensified. “It wasn’t right for Larry and I to stay married because I didn’t know what I was doing. Hadn’t figured out who I was. And he shouldn’t be suffering through that either,” King said. “I kept pleading with him to divorce me and he wouldn’t.”

item.title: Senegal re-crowned Afcon champions after appeal upheld
item.description: Senegal have been re-crowned the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations champions after the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) unanimously upheld their appeal against the decision to strip them of their title on Tuesday. Senegal contested Confederation of African Football's (Caf) decision to declare Morocco champions , wiping the Teranga Lions’ title from the records despite winning January’s Afcon final 1-0 after extra time in Rabat. The final was fraught with controversy after Senegal staged a walk-off in protest to an injury-time penalty was awarded against them in the dying stages of normal time, with players ordered into the dressing room by manager Pape Thiaw , where they remained for 14 minutes. Play was eventually resumed before Morocco’s Brahim Diaz missed the spot-kick, sailing a tame ‘Panenka’ effort into the arms of Edouard Mendy. Senegal went on to win the match in extra time through Pape Gueye. Brahim Diaz missed the penalty after Senegal staged a 14-minute walk-off (AFP/Getty) However, they were stripped of the title two months later after Caf’s Appeal Board ruled that Senegal had forfeited ⁠the match by walking off the pitch, overturning the result and awarding a 3-0 ​victory to ⁠Morocco. Senegal quickly followed with an appeal to sport's highest court, Cas, which was lodged on 25 March and have now successfully fought their case to be reinstated as champions, with the original 1-0 result restored. The three-man Cas ‌panel, presided over by French sports law ​expert Gerald Simon with assistance from ‌Italian international law professor ⁠Luigi Fumagalli and Hamburg-based ⁠attorney Ulrich Haas, ‌unanimously found that referee Jean-Jacques Ndala “did not commit any error of law”, said Cas secretary general Matthieu Reeb. Ndala’s decision to resume the match after Senegal’s walk-off fell within his sole authority and was therefore covered by the “field of play” doctrine, something Morocco’s federation argued was not the case. The court published its reasoning in a press release issued on Tuesday afternoon, which read: “By blowing his whistle to restart play, the referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met – both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume. “In the panel’s view, there is no doubt that the effects of the referee’s decision were limited to the pitch.” The panel clarified that Articles 82 and 84 of Caf’s tournament regulations, cited in the Moroccan federation’s appeal, apply only to determining match results if team conduct forces a referee to permanently call off a game, and were therefore not applicable in this instance. "In conclusion, the panel considers that in resuming the match, the referee did not err in law," a court press release added. item.title: Lakers’ Cameron Carr Reveals The Two Best Perks Of Being An NBA Player
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images Los Angeles Lakers guard Cameron Carr saw his lifelong dream come true in 2026 as he finally made it to the NBA. While playing in the league is special in itself, the players also enjoy many perks, and Carr shared the two biggest ones for him at shootaround on Monday. “I’ll probably say NBA League Pass,” Carr said, via Dave McMenamin. “Got NBA League Pass for free. Never had NBA League Pass. So that s***’s great… They do the Sleep Number stuff for the rookies. Like a discount code or something. That’s great… I’m a big sleep guy. Like, as soon as I get done with this, I’m gonna shower, go home, and take a nap.” The base version of the NBA League Pass costs $109.99 for an entire season in the U.S., while the premium one is $159.99. Carr signed a four-year, $16.8 million rookie-scale contract with the Lakers, but still views the free League Pass as a great perk because he never had it before. The 22-year-old also greatly appreciates getting a discount code for Sleep Number, the smart mattress brand. Carr saying he’s a “big sleep guy” might sound funny, but sleep is extremely important for athletes. It’s as vital as nutrition and training. Not sleeping right adversely affects an athlete’s performance, and it’s great that Carr recognizes its importance. His father, Chris Carr, is a former NBA player and might have provided guidance on this matter. The elder Carr was a journeyman who played six seasons in the NBA, and the younger one could potentially have a far better career. The New York Knicks selected him with the No. 24 pick in the 2026 NBA Draft and then traded him to the Lakers. Carr impressed at Summer League and at the start of preseason, but then the injury bug struck. He suffered a right oblique strain that kept him out of the end of preseason and the first six games of the regular season. Carr would finally make his long-awaited debut in the Lakers’ 131-125 win over the Toronto Raptors on Nov. 1. The former Baylor star didn’t get much game time at first and has even spent time in the G League , but he has gotten more minutes lately. Carr had nine points in 10 minutes in the Lakers’ 109-94 win over the Utah Jazz at Crypto.com Arena on Monday. item.title: Cameron Smith wants PGA Tour return after LIV Golf collapse, but road back won’t be easy
item.description: Cameron Smith wants back on the PGA Tour. Getting there, however, could be the hard part. The 2022 British Open champion acknowledged Tuesday that the PGA Tour is where he wants to play again, even as current Tour players have made it clear they aren't interested in rolling out the red carpet for LIV Golf defectors looking to return. “(The PGA Tour) is where I want to be now, for sure,” Smith told the Sydney Morning Herald . “There’s plenty of good players out there and plenty of other guys that want to do the same thing, so it’s going to be difficult.” Smith’s change of direction comes after the collapse of LIV Golf. The Saudi-backed league is shutting down and liquidating its remaining assets after B.C. Partners backed out of a proposed $300 million investment designed to keep LIV afloat and fund a restructuring. And if former LIV players were hoping their PGA Tour peers might be sympathetic to their predicament, the early indications suggest otherwise. News of LIV’s demise broke during the PGA Tour’s World Wide Technology Championship at El Cardonal at Diamante, an event that moved to Los Cabos after former host Mayakoba Resort partnered with LIV. Among the PGA Tour players competing there, there wasn’t much sympathy for those suddenly looking for a way back. Erik van Rooyen summed up his feelings in four words: “Go back to Q-school.” “We were told initially that if you played LIV, you would be banned from the PGA Tour, and the story just kept changing,” van Rooyen said. “They gave the finger to the Tour. If you’re that good, go get it done.” Smith’s situation is particularly interesting because he already had an opportunity to return. He was one of four players eligible for the PGA Tour’s hastily created Returning Member Program in January. Brooks Koepka took advantage of that pathway, which included a $5 million charitable donation and the loss of player equity participation for five years. Smith, Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm opted to remain with LIV. Now Smith has to find another way back. With former LIV players facing a one-year PGA Tour ban from the date of their most recent LIV appearance, Smith is turning to the DP World Tour to begin rebuilding his career. DeChambeau and Rahm have committed to full DP World Tour schedules next season, while Smith is among nine former LIV players who signed agreements giving them invitations to a specific number of DP World Tour events. Smith’s comeback begins Thursday in Sydney at the BMW Australian PGA Championship, the opening event of the DP World Tour’s new season. There is plenty of work to do. Smith was one of the best players in the world when he left for LIV, but he hasn’t come close to maintaining that form. The Cincinnati Bengals suffered a heartbreaking loss to the Washington Commanders on a walk-off field goal in their Week 11 Monday Night Football matchup. The defeat brought their five-game winning streak to an end in the most painful fashion, but Ja’Marr Chase had a pointed response when asked about the team’s disappointing performance. Though the loss was frustrating for Cincinnati, Chase didn’t hesitate to express his belief that the Bengals had the talent to win the matchup. “Losing when you know you’re better, I think that’s the worst,” Chase said. However, Washington quarterback Jayden Daniels quickly led his offense down the field before Drew Stevens sealed the Commanders’ victory with a game-winning 26-yard field goal as time expired. Despite the disappointing result, Chase remained confident that Cincinnati could take lessons from the defeat rather than allow it to derail the team’s progress. “One loss doesn’t determine anything. item.title: Senegal reinstated as Afcon 2025 winners by court ruling
item.description: Sadio Mane's Senegal have been confirmed as Afcon 2025 winners following their appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport, giving the Teranga Lions a second continental title [Getty Images] Senegal have been reinstated as winners of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) after a ruling by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas). The court's award overturns a previous decision which had stripped the West Africans of the title they won on the pitch during a chaotic final against host nation Morocco in January. The result of that match in Rabat, which saw the Teranga Lions triumph 1-0 after extra time, was overturned almost two months later when a Confederation of African Football (Caf) appeals board decreed Senegal had breached competition regulations by leaving the field of play in second-half stoppage time in protest at a penalty awarded against them. Senegal's football federation (FSF) subsequently appealed to Cas, sport's highest legal authority, with a three-man panel hearing its case behind closed doors in Lausanne on 8 October. In a unanimous verdict, the Cas panel has effectively backed the decision by referee Jean-Jacques Ndala to restart the game after Senegal returned to the field and the match was played to a conclusion. The result of the final stands and Senegal are now confirmed as Afcon 2025 winners. The court said it considered that "the referee's decision to resume the match or to stop it fell definitively within his sole authority". "By blowing his whistle to restart play, the referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met - both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume." The FSF immediately reacted with a social media post featuring a picture of the side lifting the trophy in January captioned with the phrase "again and always". Caf is yet to comment on the decision but its president Patrice Motsepe has repeatedly said that his organisation will respect and adhere to the Cas ruling. Morocco's football federation (FRMF) is also yet to comment on the verdict. 'Shameful' and 'terrible look' - the chaos that marred Afcon 2025 final 'The longest VAR check in history' - the fallout from shock Afcon decision Morocco and Senegal have both changed coach since the final and earlier this month secured their places at the 2027 edition of the tournament with two rounds of qualification remaining. This ruling should now settle any debate about who the history books will recognise as continental champions - although plenty in Morocco may not agree with the outcome of the case at Cas. item.description: Mandatory Credit: Daniel Dunn-Imagn Images We’ve seen enough from the San Antonio Spurs this season to know they remain the same championship contenders as last year. They’re 15-3 after beating the Kings 123-107 on Monday, Victor Wembanyama is having an MVP-caliber season , and the backcourt of De’Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle has been working very well. But the Spurs have also lost Dylan Harper to a left hip injury , while Tobias Harris is still waiting to make his season debut due to a left calf strain. And with the way this team has started the season, I wouldn’t be surprised if the front office looked for some help before the trade deadline . One team I’d call right now is the Los Angeles Clippers , who are 4-12 and 13th in the Western Conference after losing 116-104 to the Rockets on Monday. They have some veterans who could help other teams, including Derrick Jones Jr . and Brook Lopez , who’s somehow having one of his best offensive seasons in years at 38 years old. The Spurs have enough players and draft assets to put together an offer without touching their young stars, so let’s see how a trade for both Clippers veterans could work. The Trade Proposal San Antonio Spurs Receive: Derrick Jones Jr., Brook Lopez Los Angeles Clippers Receive: Luke Kornet, Harrison Barnes, Carter Bryant, 2028 first-round pick (via Celtics, swap rights) Jones is making $10.5 million this season, while Lopez is on a $9.2 million expiring contract. The Spurs would send around $23.6 million in salaries between their three players, with the final deal depending on the Clippers’ salary-cap restrictions. The 2028 first-round pick comes from the Derrick White deal back in 2022, as the Spurs have swap rights involving the Celtics’ selection in 2028. item.title: Freddy Peralta Predicted To Sign With Rays Over Blue Jays, Cubs, Other Suitors
item.description: Free agent pitcher Freddy Peralta Freddy Peralta is the top remaining starting pitcher on the open market, and there are a few teams that have been linked to him. According to The Athletic's Ken Rosenthal and Will Sammon , the Tampa Bay Rays, Chicago Cubs, Chicago White Sox, Toronto Blue Jays and San Diego Padres are known suitors for Peralta. Bleacher Report's Erik Beaston predicted the Rays would re-sign him. "While there will be big-money opportunities elsewhere, the Rays are a team set up to run it back in the AL and compete for another World Series," wrote Beaston. "The other teams mentioned are still a few pieces away, even with Peralta. That could prove to be a deciding factor in where the 30-year-old continues his career." The Rays are not known as huge spenders, but they could make an exception for Peralta, who was phenomenal for them. Peralta is viewed as the top priority for the Blue Jays, per MLB Network's Jom Morosi . The Cubs have had "extensive talks" with him, per USA Today's Bob Nightengale . The Padres were one of the teams involved in the Skubal sweepstakes, and the White Sox are in desperate need of starting pitching. However, the Rays have the inside edge when it comes to Peralta. Peralta has already said he wants to return to the Rays. The Cubs have already agreed to a deal with Trevor Rogers, so they may not be as aggressive in pursuit of Peralta. However, the Blue Jays, Padres and White Sox still have plenty of reasons to try to get him. There may be more teams trying to get him as well, but among the known suitors, the Rays could have a leg up. item.description: The New York Giants helped themselves immensely in the race to the NFC East title with their 23-18 victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday. Unfortunately for the Giants, the rest of the division kept pace. The 5-6 Dallas Cowboys overwhelmed the hapless Tennessee Titans, the Philadelphia Eagles upset the Pittsburgh Steelers, and perhaps most importantly in the big picture the Washington Commanders upset the Cincinnati Bengals 22-20 on Monday Night Football. item.title: Senegal regain AFCON title after appeal to sports court
item.description: Sadio Mane holds up the AFCON trophy after Senegal's 1-0 extra-time win over hosts Morocco in the final in January (SEBASTIEN BOZON) Senegal on Tuesday regained their Africa Cup of Nations title after winning an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) against the decision by the Confederation of African Football to declare Morocco the winners following a chaotic final in January. "The Court of Arbitration for Sport has upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF) concerning the final of the Africa Cup of Nations Morocco 2025," CAS said in a statement. The Swiss-based sports court said Senegal's appeal had been upheld by "a unanimous decision", and their original 1-0 victory after extra time is reinstated. In March, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) sensationally overturned the result of the final, awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory, and the title, after many Senegalese players walked off the pitch in protest at a penalty given to the hosts with the game still goalless. The CAF Appeals Committee had justified its decision to overturn the result and declare Morocco champions based on Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations. Those state that if a team "refuses to play or leaves the ground before the regular end of the match without the authorisation of the referee, it shall be considered (loser) and shall be eliminated for good from the current competition". However, the Senegal players eventually returned to the pitch and the final carried on. The CAS panel therefore considered that the referee's decision to restart the final showed that "the conditions for resuming the match had been met", and that articles 82 and 84 were therefore "not applicable in this case". elm-obo/dar/as/mw

item.title: Red Wings Chaos Delayed Larkin Deal
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect According to Dylan Larkin’s agent, the chaos that erupted within the Detroit Red Wings organization over the summer months derailed any hope of an early resolution to Larkin’s trade request. Appearing on Sportsnet, Pat Brisson acknowledged that Larkin first issued his trade demand to the Red Wings in May. "Teams were calling the Red Wings when no one was in charge… It was a very frustrating process." Dylan Larkin's agent, Pat Brisson, joins @RealKyper and @jtbourne to go behind the scenes on the deal. pic.twitter.com/mXshuYfOtT — Sportsnet (@Sportsnet) November 23, 2026 “Once we made it official in May when Dylan requested a trade, we’re hoping for this to happen before the draft because it’s always a better time of the year for these things to happen,” Brisson said. “A lot of moving parts. “That’s when teams are rebuilt for the most part. And then once we passed July 1st and Steve [ Yzerman ] was let go [as GM] on July 14th, it made it very, very complicated for us and for Detroit to operate. “Teams were calling the Red Wings with offers, and there was no one in charge officially.” Red Wings Summer of Discontent Put Larkin in Limbo While the Red Wings fiddled over their future direction throughout the summer, Brisson and Larkin were left to stew on the sideline. And any chance for a quick resolution to what became a festering sore for the Red Wings was gone. “It was a very frustrating process because July and August were two dead months, so to speak,” Brisson said. “I was hoping that at that point they’d have a leadership group in place so we could have had conversations and progressive conversations in order to try to get it done. “But it didn’t happen.” Instead, the Red Wings waited until the eve of training camp in September to install Shawn Horcoff as interim GM. “Shawn Horcoff only became the interim GM two days before camp in September,” Brisson said. “It’s a very tough time to move an asset because teams are ready for camp. They want to try their young guys. They’re fulfilled. “Everyone’s winning the Cup at that time.” Instead, it took until Sunday, November 22, to finally resolve Larkin’s request when he was dealt to the Montreal Canadiens. Seven months after his request was initially made. item.title: How would a deal like Tarik Skubal’s work under a salary cap?
item.description: Last week at the MLB owners meetings, Commissioner Rob Manfred said this : “I can’t imagine the owners ratifying a deal that does not include a cap and floor.” Okay. So that’s probably posturing and not what’s actually going to happen whenever MLB owners and the MLBPA reach a deal. But it’s out there. So let’s look at some things that could happen going forward. At Forbes, Maury Brown has written about what a deal like the one Tarik Skubal has agreed to with the Mets might do under such a cap/floor system, and the problem is summed up this way: Under MLB’s latest economic proposal, a salary cap and floor system would start in 2028. Accounting for present-day values, eight players would consume 92% of the Mets’ cap allocation for that year. It remains unknown how multi-year contracts extending past 2028 would be handled if a cap is implemented. So there’s the issue in a nutshell. Not every team has contracts like the Skubal deal, or the Juan Soto deal also eating up a lot of the Mets’ payroll, but what would happen going forward where contracts like that would push a team way over any cap proposal? Brown writes about two ways things could go for MLB. First, he mentions the NHL and how they lost an entire season arguing about a salary cap, which was eventually instituted. And before you say that can’t happen in MLB — yes, it absolutely could. Here’s what happened in the NHL: To start, all remaining contracts were rolled back 24% for the 2004-05 season. Contracts on the books after that were simply voided. Additionally, the rollback also hit players who had to be given qualifying offers for new deals. Those qualifying offers were based on a player’s salary in his last contracted year, minus the 24% rollback. This seems like an extraordinary leap for MLB players to make, but it does show that a rollback has been done in the past. I believe Brown is correct that this would be “an extraordinary leap for MLB players to make.” The other way is to grandfather pre-cap contracts, as the NBA did when they instituted their cap system. That worked this way: One scenario would be for all existing multiyear contracts past 2028 to be honored, likely with the league moving off a hard cap and to a soft cap. This follows what the NBA did in 2005: contracts signed prior to the new deal were honored as written—there were no rollbacks or voids to existing salaries. The NBA also allowed for contracts of four or more seasons to be renegotiated (for teams under the cap) after the third anniversary of signing, extending, or a prior renegotiation that raised any season’s salary by more than 8%, while contracts under four years could not be renegotiated. To me, this would seem the most likely scenario. It also would explain why Steve Cohen lavished that contract on Skubal. There are only two explanations here: 1) Cohen figures there won’t be a cap, or 2) Cohen figures this contract (and Soto’s) would be grandfathered. item.description: I’ve spent an inordinate amount of time studying this Bills and Chiefs Thanksgiving game, digging deep for specific exploitable tendencies, team and player trends entering the contest, and anything I could find that could hint at who or what may swing this heavyweight bout. In this enormous but expedited process, it dawned on me — these teams are ridiculously similar. Maybe not in every way imaginable, of course. But they’re entering this contest about as close to being mirror images as we’ll see in the NFL, particularly for two Super Bowl contenders. Josh Allen. Patrick Mahomes. James Cook. Kenneth Walker. Cook is third in the NFL in rushing yards per game at 106. Walker is second at 109. These teams are each coming off three-straight wins over 17 or more points, which marks the first occurrence of a matchup between clubs entering a contest against each other with those type of win streaks since 2007 when the 8-0 Patriots — yes, those Patriots — traveled to Indianapolis to face the 7-0 Colts. (shoutout Doug Clawson for that stat) Both teams have sturdy, veteran-laden offensive lines. How about the pass games? The Bills are currently third in non-garbage time EPA per dropback at +0.213. The Chiefs are fifth at +0.194. Buffalo has the league’s eighth-best third-down conversion rate at 42.6%. Kansas City isn’t far behind, in 10th at 41.8%. Andy Reid’s club has converted 65.8% of their red-zone trips to touchdowns, the eighth-best in the NFL. The Bills have scored a touchdown on 63.4% of their trips into the red zone, which is the league’s 12th-highest. Points per drive? Bills are currently in fourth at 2.86, while the Chiefs are seventh at 2.50. Overall offensive success rate? item.title: 2026 Dodgers season review: Max Muncy
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 21: Max Muncy #13 of the Los Angeles Dodgers celebrates his two run home run, to take a 2-1 lead over the Pittsburgh Pirates, during the first inning at Dodger Stadium on August 21, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images An underrated aspect of how the Dodgers have managed to stay at and near the top for so long is how their veteran players seem to age so gracefully. And perhaps, no player better embodies that than Max Muncy, who shows no signs of slowing down at 36 years of age, coming off one of his better seasons in a long time. It’s not only because he’s been healthier, setting a new career high in games played with 149, but also because he’s still with top-notch production, near the top of the team’s leaderboards in most offensive categories. On a per-rate basis, Muncy was coming off productive campaigns, but injuries limited him to just 86.5 games per season between 2024 and 2025. It was a different story this past season, as one of the more reliable hitters on the top team was in the top 3 in both runs scored (81) and RBI (76). Interestingly, while Pages took advantage of Ohtani’s down year with the bat to accomplish an unlikely feat in leading the team in RBI, Muncy had a similar opportunity with the long ball. However, the veteran fell just shy of it with 29 homers, one fewer than Ohtani. Early in the year, though, Muncy was all about the multihomer game, noting that three of the first four games he left the yard in were all multihomer games—including a three-homer day against the Rangers, one you’ll read more about in the Game of the Year section. Surprisingly, it was only Muncy’s second three-homer game and first one in nearly two years, repeating a feat he first accomplished against the Braves in 2024. Those multihomer games laid the foundation for what would be a productive season, but they often came with a minimized impact, as each of Muncy’s first eight home runs were all solo shots—helping explain why he entered May with more extra-base hits (13) than RBI (11). An impressive first half helped Muncy earn his third All-Star appearance, but more importantly, the first one as a starter, beating Alec Bohm in the process. Not short of talent at the position in recent years, it had been a while since the Dodgers last sent the starter at third to the All-Star game, nearly half a century. Prior to Muncy, Ron Cey, in 1977, was the last Dodger third baseman to feature in the starting lineup for the NL in an All-Star Game. As if to celebrate this achievement, Muncy returned for the second half with one of his most impactful games of the regular season, securing a homer and two-RBI in the Dodgers’ narrow 2-1 victory over the Yankees. Taking Gerrit Cole deep in the 7th inning of a game in which your team trails 1-0 in the meeting of baseball’s two biggest franchises is a special moment, even for a veteran. item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. On Friday, Kuntz was already speaking of the team in the past tense. “I really enjoyed my time at the Galaxy. I love being here,” he said. “I’d like to be back if it was up to me. item.description: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟 Philadelphia Union and USMNT midfielder Cavan Sullivan has capped a record-setting regular season by being named the 2026 MLS Young Player of the Year. At 17 years and two days old, he became the youngest winner of the award in league history. His production on the club level soon translated to the international stage. Sullivan received his first call-up to the US men's national team in September and made his debut against Peru, becoming the second-youngest player in USMNT history to start a match. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
